drawings.label: Woodland Hills 121 degrees Fahrenheit in 2020, the previous county record of 119 in 2006, and Burbank at 114 in 2020.
drawings.caption: Official air-temperature readings from the L.A. Times report on the September 2020 heat wave, plotted on an axis that starts at 110 °F so the gaps are visible. Burbank’s reading was reported as appearing to tie its all-time record.
drawings.heading: 01One reading, and what it cannot tell you

drawings.label: A person stands on paving. A thermometer shows air temperature. Arrows show sun hitting the person and heat radiating up from the paving.
drawings.caption: A weather station reports air temperature. A person on a sidewalk also takes sun on the skin and heat from the surfaces around them. Concept sketch, not a measurement.
drawings.heading: 04Air temperature is not what a body feels

drawings.label: Air temperature reductions of up to 3.5, 2.1 and 0.5 degrees Fahrenheit; surface temperature reductions of about 10 and an average of 12.8 degrees.
drawings.caption: Pacoima, where over 700,000 sq ft of dark asphalt was coated in summer 2022. Air and surface temperatures are different quantities on different scales, so read each panel on its own. Values are the maximum (“up to”) reductions the study reported, not averages, except the city figure. Sources 1
drawings.heading: 02What it found

drawings.label: A small square tree well sits at the center of a much larger square of soil, which sits inside a dashed circle for a thirty foot crown.
drawings.caption: Plan view at one scale: the soil a mature shade tree is commonly said to need, set against a small tree well. The 1,000 cu ft figure is a rule of thumb, and 48 cu ft is my assumed size for a small well. Arithmetic: 1,000 ÷ 3 ft = 333 sq ft, about 18 × 18 ft. Concept sketch.
drawings.heading: 03The tree well next to it

drawings.label: A cross section of a street, curb, planting strip with a tree, a sidewalk 48 inches wide with a two percent cross slope, and a building. A dimension line marks the clear width.
drawings.caption: The three numbers that shape most sidewalk design under the federal guidelines: clear width, cross slope, and the step between slabs. A tree trunk or pole inside the 48 in is a defect, not a feature. Concept sketch.
drawings.heading: 02The three numbers that shape a sidewalk

drawings.label: Two identical straight routes of 1,320 feet. The first is bare. The second has trees along it, with shaded stretches under the crowns.
drawings.caption: A quarter mile is 1,320 ft however it feels. What changes is how much of it is in the sun. The tree positions are illustrative, not a real street. Concept sketch.
drawings.heading: 02What a quarter mile is
